entries.value: The nursery raises the colony's young bees. Feed the brood regularly to raise its nutrition — once it's well fed, you can train a new worker. The more workers your hive has, the more tasks it can handle at once, which speeds up progress everywhere else in the hive.

Honey is the colony's core energy resource — it pays for most actions (feeding, training, upgrades). This building produces honey continuously, but nothing is credited automatically: tap the building to manually collect what has piled up, up to its storage capacity. Upgrade it to increase both production and capacity.

The guard post trains the guardians that defend your hive and form your combat patrols on the world map. The higher its level, the more guardians you can field at once and the more patrols you can run simultaneously. Without a developed guard post, your colony stays vulnerable to attacks.

The warehouse stores pollen gathered by your foragers, a resource used for colony growth and certain research. Like honey and wax, pollen accumulates in the building but must be collected manually by tapping it — nothing is added to your reserves automatically.

The workshop turns raw materials into wax, used to build and reinforce hive cells and for many upgrades. Like honey and pollen, wax produced here must be collected manually once it has accumulated, by tapping the building directly.

The research lab lets you unlock studies that permanently improve your colony: higher production, better storage capacity, stronger efficiency. Each study costs resources and takes time to complete, but once finished its effect stays active forever — unlike the temporary effects of a one-time upgrade.

The administration core is the heart of your hive: it gathers general information about your colony, such as its identity and overall progress. It's a good reference point for checking your hive's overall state at a glance.
This extra defensive zone isn't available yet in this version. It will open at a future colony level, once this system is ready.
The genetics garden is an advanced research feature planned for a future update. For now, this zone remains a preview and has no real effect on your colony.
The infirmary will heal and support injured bees in a future update. No official health system is active right now — this zone is still under development.
The academy will one day let you train your bees in advanced skills, beyond basic training. This feature isn't connected to the game yet.

The bank will require a connection to an official server to manage your resources securely, like many mobile games. It isn't active yet in this local preview — no official resources are currently managed there.
The archives will one day keep a full history of your colony's events. This zone isn't persistent yet: nothing that happens here is saved for the moment.

The alliance hall will let you join other players, chat with them, and climb a shared leaderboard — like many mobile multiplayer (MMO) games. This system needs a real server shared between players, which doesn't exist yet in this version.
Assignment and growth of young bees
Every kingdom begins with a single drop.

Deep inside the old oak, a young colony awakens with nearly empty reserves. Honey feeds the bees, powers their work, and gives the hive time to grow. Gather this first nectar, then organize the workers so every drop can serve the colony's future.
Honey provides the energy needed for every early action.
A resource becomes useful when a team knows how to produce it.
The first choices set the pace of the hive's growth.
CHAPTER 2 · THE HEART OF THE NURSERY
The next generation depends on you.

In the nursery, the next generation depends on your decisions. Pollen supports brood growth, honey gives nurse bees energy, and wax protects the chambers. Observe before you act: a strong colony begins with well-fed larvae and a stable environment.
Pollen provides the essential nutrients the brood needs.
Nutrition, warmth, and stability reveal what the larvae need.
Wax strengthens the chambers where the colony develops.
A bee finds her place through action.

A young bee is ready to leave her cell. She is not born with a fixed destiny: her first duties, her mentors, and the hive's priorities will shape her specialty. Guide her carefully; every worker becomes a living part of your kingdom.
A healthy brood is the beginning of every successful emergence.
A bee's first tasks reveal her strengths.
Experience and mentoring guide her future role.
Honey sustains life. Wax makes it grow.

The colony has grown, but its chambers cannot remain primitive. Honey provides energy, wax makes construction possible, and pollen supports growth. Learn to tell what is spent from what is produced, then turn the workshop into a true engine for the hive.
Feeds, trains, and puts teams to work.
Develops the brood and specialized bees.
Protect the colony without exhausting it.

An unfamiliar presence prowls near the galleries. Defense depends on more than the number of guardians: you must observe the threat, choose a response, and preserve the reserves. Protect the brood without exhausting the colony, then build security that can endure.
A scout reveals the nature and urgency of the threat.
Each strategy commits different bees and reserves.
Lasting defenses protect the hive without stopping all its work.
The kingdom does not end at these walls.

For the first time, the colony looks beyond its walls. The outside world offers resources, allies, and dangers, but every expedition begins with a safe landmark: your hive. Learn to find it, read the territory, and return before venturing farther.
It remains the departure and return point for every expedition.
Terrain, regions, and distance transform every journey.
Knowing how to return matters as much as knowing how to leave.
The world's riches must be brought home.

The flowers across the territory are rich with pollen, but no harvest reaches the reserves on its own. Find a source, send a team, wait for its return, then claim the load. A good route enriches the hive; a poor choice ties up precious bees.
Quality, distance, and safety determine the value of the route.
Foragers remain busy until they return.
The load reaches the hive only after the final collection.

Striga held the breach at the Southern Nursery alone during the great comb collapse, protecting three broods until help arrived. She still carries a crescent-shaped scar on her left wing - and no guardian backs down in front of her anymore.
Zephyra holds the hive's speed record, linking the Warehouse to the Guard Post in under nine wingbeats, a feat no one has matched since. She now trains young wingrunners on the emergency corridors.

Ambra single-handedly repelled a scouting hornet swarm probing the outer defenses, firing twenty-three stinger volleys without ever missing her mark. Her name is now whispered among recruits as a warning to invaders.
Nectaria mapped seven new clover fields in a single season, doubling the hive's reserves before winter. Foragers still follow the routes she laid out today.
Aurelia survived a winter the hive thought it would never see the end of, rationing pollen drop by drop until the thaw. She is said to still refuse to waste the smallest crumb.
